goal: As a purchasing agent, evaluate three furniture quotations for PR-2025-0042 under a $310,000 hard cap. Deliver four files: a discrepancy/compliance audit CSV (quantity, arithmetic, spec gaps against CR-001 to CR-010, severity, actions), an adjusted bid tabulation xlsx with three scenarios, a weighted vendor scorecard xlsx using vendor_history.db, and a recommendation memo (budget analysis, CR pass/fail table, risk assessment, counter-offer, escalation path).
delivered: All four files are in output/. discrepancy_compliance_audit.csv uses Low/Medium/High severity. The tabulation's adjusted all-in totals are Meridian $378,940, Atlas $309,510 and Pinnacle $264,350. The scorecard ranks Atlas first (72.0). The memo recommends a conditional award to Atlas with an Atlas counter-offer and escalation to the VP of Operations; its CR table treats 'pending evidence' as Fail.
what_went_wrong: The memo's risk and evaluation text stays generic. It omits Pinnacle's claim #9 weld crack and #10 gas-cylinder drop and their injury implications. It also omits the 50% deposit details and the 2-3 week CFO-review delay from the budget memo, Meridian's 5% conference discount, and Meridian-specific negotiation targets. Several facts the subagents had returned were dropped from the deliverables: Meridian's 2 claims resolved in 7/9 days, Atlas's 4 claims with 1 denied, and 2-drawer cabinets from all three vendors (the audit flags Meridian only). Three items failed only because mandatory failures were labelled 'High' rather than 'Critical', a label the task never specifies. Two items expected Meridian to pass CR-008 and CR-005/010 even though conference-chair ratings and phased-delivery confirmation are absent from its quote.

failed_items.why: Atlas 60K and Pinnacle 45K CR-005 fails and the Meridian 100K pass are all correct. The only miss is severity 'High' instead of 'Critical' (AUD-077/087); the task says only 'include severity classification' and gives no scale.

CR-006 fails for Atlas (27.5 in) and Pinnacle (28 in) and the Meridian pass (25.5 in) are correct. It failed only because AUD-078/088 say 'High', not 'Critical', a label the prompt and files never require.

The Pinnacle 250 lb fail is correct. The rubric wants Meridian and Atlas confirmed as passing, but CR-008 covers task AND conference chairs and no quote states a conference-chair capacity. The agent's 'Verify' (AUD-070/080) follows compliance_requirements.csv; the rubric ignores the conference-chair scope.
Pinnacle's 'Partial shipments not available' is correctly flagged as a CR-010 Fail (AUD-092). The item failed only for using 'High' instead of 'Critical' severity, which the task does not specify.

Subagent b4e2d178 reported 'A ... 2 claims (both resolved, 7/9 days)' and 'B ... 4 claims (one denied, all closed)'. The root's scorecard and memo give only '0 open claims' for both, so the historical-claims contrast never reached the graded files.

The Pinnacle quote states the 50% deposit is due at PO with 50% on delivery and becomes non-refundable after production starts. budget_amendment_memo item 4 states the Net 30/45 preference and a possible 2-3 week CFO delay. The root read both, but the memo says only '50% deposit creates CFO risk'.

The $378,940 total and $68,940 overage plus VP Ops escalation are stated. The counter-offer is Atlas-only and the memo never clearly says Meridian cannot be brought under the cap. The Meridian 5% conference discount (~$3,027) appeared in the subagent's result but was left out of the memo.

The Atlas and Pinnacle fail lists match the rubric. Meridian is shown 'Fail (pending evidence)' on CR-005, CR-008 and CR-010 because its conference chairs have unrated vinyl and no stated capacity, and its quote gives no written phased-delivery confirmation (CR-010 requires 'written confirmation'). This is evidence-based; the rubric assumes passes the quote does not support.

warranty_claims holds #9 (PO-2024-0205, weld crack, desk unstable) and #10 (PO-2024-0680, gas cylinder drop while occupied), and the agent queried that table. The memo only says '2 open safety/structural claims' and never names the incidents or explains the occupant-injury and workplace-hazard implications.

Subagent b4e2d178 flagged '2-drawer vs 3 (HIGH)' for all three vendors and suggested a Facilities waiver. The root's audit includes only AUD-019 for Meridian; the Atlas and Pinnacle cabinet rows check quantity and arithmetic only.

subagent_notes: Two background subagents ran: 6ff22f4d (bid math and negotiation) and b4e2d178 (independent compliance audit plus vendor-history aggregates). Their numbers were accurate and fed the tabulation and scorecard. Several of their correct details were dropped when the root wrote the deliverables (claim histories, 2-drawer for Atlas/Pinnacle, the 5% Meridian discount), costing 16 points as L. 6ff22f4d also proposed Atlas as the conditional winner, which the root adopted and which led to the Atlas-only counter-offer.
